title: Roxane Gay Inspires at Harvard's Peggy Schmertzler Leadership Seminar: Key Insights and Highlights
text:
Roxane Gay Urges Students to Define Feminism Themselves at Harvard seminar Roxane Gay, the acclaimed author and social commentator, addressed a packed audience at the Harvard Faculty Club on Feb. 12, 2025, during the Harvard College Women’s Center’s annual Schmertzler Leadership Seminar.Gay challenged attendees to move beyond defining feminism and rather focus on enacting meaningful change.More than a decade after her influential work, “Bad Feminist,” Gay emphasized the importance of individual action and critical thinking in shaping a more equitable world. Her insights into the writing process, the perils of social media, and the evolving landscape of feminist literature resonated deeply with the students and faculty present.
Moving Beyond Definitions: A Call to action Gay’s central message revolved around shifting the focus from endless debates about the definition of feminism to concrete actions that drive progress. She stated emphatically, “It’s 2025, if you don’t have a credible answer to that question, that’s a ‘you’ problem. It’s not for me to solve it.” This direct challenge urged students to take ownership of their understanding of feminism and apply it to real-world issues.
She further elaborated on the necessity of making tough choices to achieve desired change. “At some point, we have to ask ourselves, what kinds of difficult choices are we going to be willing to make to create the change that we want to see in the world? We have to sometimes consider making the difficult sacrifices. Of course, we do what we can within the constraints of our life,” gay shared, highlighting the complexities and compromises often involved in activism and social progress.
Insights into Gay’s Writing Process The seminar, facilitated by dulce gonzalez Arias ’26 and Olivia data ’26, provided a platform for attendees to gain insights into gay’s creative process. Bonnie Talbert, interim Director of the Women’s Center, emphasized that these discussions are part of the center’s ongoing efforts to empower women as effective leaders.gay revealed that mental writing drafts are her preferred method, allowing her to refine her ideas before committing them to paper.
Reflecting on her early aspirations, Gay noted the importance of encouragement and support. “I am someone who’s been writing since I was four years old and I took myself very seriously as a writer,even at four. Fortunately, I have parents who also took me seriously as a writer,” she said. “When you have someone that takes you seriously and believes that you can do the things that you want to do, even when they know realistically that it’s pretty hard to make it as any sort of creative person, it really does help.” This underscored the profound impact of early validation on nurturing creative talent.
Navigating the Digital Age: A Warning about Social Media Gay also addressed the pervasive influence of social media,cautioning against its potential to consume and control.She urged attendees to limit their engagement with platforms like X (formerly Twitter),stating, “We’re really in a problematic age right now with social media. Don’t give them any power. When you give them your access,when you give them your data,you are giving them power.” This warning highlighted the importance of maintaining control over one’s digital footprint and resisting the addictive nature of these platforms.
“The Portable Feminist Reader”: A contemporary Update Attendees also gained insight into Gay’s forthcoming publication, “The Portable Feminist Reader,” scheduled for release in March. This compilation of feminist texts traditionally focuses on classic works. Gay noted that previous editions were “historically very white,very heterosexual,and very middle class.” The newest version seeks to broaden the scope by including a diverse range of contemporary voices.
Gay explained her approach to curating the collection: “I tried to find a balance between contemporary work that I find incredibly exciting” and classical texts like “The Yellow Wallpaper” by charlotte Perkins Gilman. This blend of established and emerging voices aims to provide a thorough and inclusive overview of feminist thought.
Practical Career Advice for Aspiring Creatives Concluding her talk, Gay offered practical advice for those pursuing careers in creative fields: secure a day job. “I’ve always had a day job,and that’s what has afforded me the ability to write whatever I want to write,” she explained. “I could take chances, because my livelihood, my rent, etcetera was not being paid by opinions.” This pragmatic approach emphasizes the importance of financial independence in fostering artistic freedom and allowing creators to pursue their passions without compromising their vision.
Conclusion Roxane Gay’s appearance at the Harvard College Women’s Center’s Schmertzler Leadership seminar provided invaluable insights into feminism,the writing process,and navigating the complexities of the modern world. Her call to action, urging students to define feminism for themselves and focus on creating tangible change, resonated deeply with the audience. By sharing her personal experiences and offering practical advice, Gay empowered attendees to pursue their passions with purpose and conviction.
roxane Gay’s Call to Action: Redefining Feminism for a New Generation “Feminism isn’t a destination; it’s a continuous evolution, a dynamic process of challenging norms and advocating for equity.” This powerful statement, echoing the sentiments of author Roxane Gay, encapsulates the evolving landscape of feminist thought.To delve deeper into this vital conversation, we spoke with Dr. Evelyn Reed,a renowned professor of Gender Studies and author of The Evolving Face of Feminism .
World-Today-News.com: Dr. Reed, roxane Gay’s recent seminar emphasized moving beyond rigid definitions of feminism towards concrete action. How important is this shift in the contemporary feminist discourse?
Dr.Reed: Gay’s call to action is incredibly significant. For too long, the feminist movement has been bogged down in internal debates over terminology and theoretical frameworks. While these intellectual exercises have their place, they frequently overshadow the urgent need for tangible progress on issues like gender pay gaps, reproductive rights, and systemic discrimination. Shifting the focus towards action—towards enacting meaningful change in our communities—is crucial to revitalizing feminism and making it truly relevant to a new generation. This isn’t about abandoning theoretical exploration, but prioritizing the practical applications of feminist ideals.
From Theory to Practice: Embracing Actionable Feminism World-Today-News.com: Gay also stressed the importance of making difficult choices for social change. Can you elaborate on the challenges and compromises inherent in feminist activism?
Dr. Reed: Activism, particularly within the feminist movement, rarely follows a straightforward path. It requires navigating complex social,political,and economic landscapes. Making difficult choices frequently enough involves strategic compromises—choosing battles wisely, prioritizing certain objectives over others, and adapting strategies to suit diverse contexts. The history of feminism is rich with examples of these compromises – from the suffrage movement’s gradual expansions of rights to the ongoing debates about intersectionality and inclusivity. Accomplished feminist activism demands both courageous action and a measured approach.
World-Today-News.com: Gay’s seminar also touched upon the challenges of social media and its influence on feminist discourse. How can activists best navigate this digital landscape?
Dr. Reed: Social media presents both opportunities and pitfalls for feminist activism. On one hand, it provides powerful tools for organizing, disseminating facts, and amplifying diverse voices.Though, it also harbors echo chambers, misinformation campaigns, and online harassment. Effective navigation requires a strategic approach: carefully selecting platforms, fostering constructive engagement, building strong online communities, and deploying media literacy skills to discern fact from fiction. Importantly, maintaining a healthy balance between online and offline activism is essential to preserve mental well-being and build sustainable movements.
Cultivating the next Generation of Feminist Leaders World-Today-News.com: Gay’s emphasis on personal obligation and individual action is noteworthy. How can young people be empowered to define feminism for themselves and contribute to a more equitable world?
Dr. Reed: Empowering young people requires fostering critical thinking, encouraging self-reflection, and cultivating a sense of agency. This involves:
Education: Providing comprehensive and inclusive education on gender studies, social justice, and feminist history. Mentorship: Connecting young people with established feminist leaders and activists. Creating Safe Spaces: Establishing platforms for open dialog, respectful debate, and collaborative action. Promoting Leadership Progress: Equipping young people with the skills and confidence to lead social change movements. World-Today-News.com: Gay’s discussion of her upcoming book, “The Portable Feminist Reader,” highlights the need for diverse and inclusive feminist narratives. How vital is it to broaden the scope of canonical feminist texts?
Dr. Reed: Expanding the canon of feminist literature is absolutely crucial to ensuring depiction and fostering a more inclusive movement. Conventional collections have often centered on voices from a narrow range of backgrounds and experiences. By incorporating diverse voices and perspectives, we can gain a richer understanding of feminist thought and build a stronger, more effective movement. It’s about creating a more complete and authentic picture of the fight for gender equality.
World-Today-News.com: Dr. Reed, thank you for these insightful perspectives.Your expertise has provided valuable context to Roxane Gay’s critically important message.
Concluding thoughts: Roxane Gay’s call to action serves as a vital reminder that feminism is not a static ideology, but a dynamic and evolving movement. By embracing individual responsibility, prioritizing concrete action, and fostering inclusivity, we can work towards a more equitable and just world.
